bullets.title: META: Citi reiterates Buy + 90-day catalyst watch; Muse hits 900K downloads, 'Watermelon' model in 2027
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on META, adds upside catalyst watch expiring Dec 15, ahead of Meta Connect (Sept 23-24). Muse personal agent reached 900K+ downloads in one week (exceeding IG/FB app downloads); META accelerated model release cadence from 13-week to 4-week cycles. Citi PT implies ~22x 2027E EPS; survey shows 45% US ownership of next-gen Meta glasses with 30% planning to buy.

bullets.title: CRM: Dreamforce strong — 30K+ Agentforce customers, $484M pipeline, $50B+ FY28 revenue target; Mizuho raises PT to $280
bullets.body: CRM Dreamforce showcased AIforce (Data 360 + Agentforce + Claude/Slack), with 30K+ Agentforce customers, 7B AWUs, and $484M annualized pipeline from Hunter/Piper. Slack added 100K+ new customers with 900% AI user growth. Mizuho raised PT to $280 (Outperform) on CY26 revenue re-acceleration; FY28 guidance implies $50B+ revenue with record-low attrition.

bullets.title: INTC +3.3% pre-market: SK Hynix in early talks on US memory chip production at Ohio facility
bullets.body: Reuters reported SK Hynix exploring leasing Intel's Ohio facility or a JV with Intel and cloud firms to manufacture memory chips in the US. SK Hynix clarified nothing is finalized; South Korean government opposition cited as hurdle. MU +0.9% on the news; White House semiconductor tariffs with relief for US investment add incentive.

bullets.title: NVDA/AI infra: AI safety requires MORE compute — Vera Rubin 30x better for agents; Citi PT $315
bullets.body: AI safety summit Day 1 consensus: alignment is compute-intensive, not compute-limiting. Nvidia Vera Rubin delivers 3x token throughput baseline, 5x post-optimization, 30x better AI factory throughput on agentic workloads (100x more demanding than 2023 chat). Citi maintains NVDA Buy at $315 (21x P/E); hyperscaler capex robust with 13% net debt/equity.

bullets.title: EXPE downgraded to Underweight at MS ($235 PT, 20% downside); BKNG OW at $230, ABNB upgraded to EW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley initiates OTA coverage: EXPE cut to UW from EW with PT slashed to $235 from $300 on US/chain-hotel/air exposure and narrowing valuation discount to BKNG (narrowest P/E gap in 4+ years). BKNG maintained OW at $230 (34% upside) on 4.7M unique properties and execution track record. ABNB upgraded to EW from UW, PT raised to $170 from $125.

bullets.title: TSLA 3Q26 deliveries cut to 435K (vs 456K consensus); 4Q guide trimmed to 475K
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs and JPM both flag TSLA 3Q deliveries tracking ~435K, below 456K consensus, with weakness across China, US, and Europe. 4Q26 guidance cut to 475K from 515K. GS rates TSLA Neutral; Hedgeye signals Bearish trend.

bullets.title: MSFT: 8% dividend hike to $0.98/qtr; ~19% EPS CAGR through CY28 supports 20% total return
bullets.body: Microsoft increased quarterly dividend 8% to $0.98/share ($3.92 annualized, 0.78% yield). MS models ~21% revenue CAGR through CY28 with OpEx growing only ~11%, implying ~19% EPS CAGR. Project Kilby (20-year power agreement with MSFT) adds long-duration data center demand exposure via CVX.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 lead times flat Y/Y (constructive early signal); Siri lags rivals on agent capabilities
bullets.body: MS reports flat Y/Y iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max lead times, suggesting healthier early premium demand than feared; prices up $100 Y/Y with $100 higher carrier subsidies. iPhone Duo delayed 5 weeks may weigh on near-term leads. Separately, AAPL Siri redesigned but lacks agent capabilities (cannot surf web or access Gmail), putting it behind ChatGPT/Claude.

bullets.title: LITE on Positive Catalyst Watch ahead of ECOC (Sept 21-24); CPO adoption timing key swing factor for COHR/LITE
bullets.body: Citi places LITE on Positive Catalyst Watch ahead of ECOC conference in Málaga (Sept 21-24). The 800G-to-1.6T transition pace and CPO migration from pluggable module to accelerator package are the primary sentiment swing factors for LITE and COHR. EML vs. CW laser technology debate for 3.2T modules remains unresolved.

bullets.title: AMZN: Project Mercury — same-day network to grow 85→1,000+ facilities by 2031; CART down 1.3%
bullets.body: Amazon plans to expand its same-day fulfillment network 10x to 1,000+ facilities by 2031 under Project Mercury. Amazon Now (~30 min delivery) launched in Atlanta, Dallas-Fort Worth, Philadelphia, and Seattle with tens of millions of customers by year-end. CART fell 1.3% pre-market on the competitive threat.

bullets.title: HOOD: CLARITY Act fails Senate; near-term negative for crypto brokers
bullets.body: The CLARITY Act failed Senate cloture by 11 votes, a near-term negative for Coinbase, Robinhood, and Gemini. SEC/CFTC rulemaking within existing authority can still advance digital-asset regulation. MS remains Underweight on Circle (CRDO) despite alternative legal routes.

bullets.title: DELL gains server share in 2Q26; HPE stable; SMCI mixed with AI server softness
bullets.body: GS notes DELL gained market share in both traditional and AI servers YoY in 2Q26; HPE market share held stable; SMCI showed mixed results with AI server softness. TMT stocks are most net bought sector among all US sectors in September with Mag 7 net allocation at ~20% (95th percentile 3-year).

bullets.title: GOOGL: UBS sees 3Q ad growth reaccelerating to ~13% YoY; META and AMZN favored for share gains
bullets.body: UBS expects 3Q ad growth to reaccelerate to ~13% YoY from political spending, budget flush, and AI-driven monetization. META and AMZN are favored for share consolidation toward scaled ad platforms. Google also accelerating its TPU cycle to 6-month cadence.

bullets.title: SNOW upgraded to Bullish; NFLX downgraded to Bearish — Hedgeye Risk Range signals
bullets.body: Hedgeye flips SNOW to Bullish trend signal and downgrades NFLX to Bearish. MSFT, AAPL, META remain Bullish; AMZN, GOOGL, TSLA signal Bearish. NVDA stays Neutral. S&P 500 bullish; Russell 2000 bearish; 10Y/30Y yields trending bullish (higher).

bullets.title: RCL best-in-class cruise; VIK reinstated as Top Pick with 30-40% upside; NCLH short bias
bullets.body: Hedgeye reinstates VIK as Top Pick on HSD-range 2026-27 yield resilience and buyback; RCL remains Best Idea #2, with Q4 pricing supporting guidance reaffirmation and Caribbean share gains via new ships (Legend late 2026, Hero H2 2027). NCLH continues underperformance with no turnaround visible. Cruise stocks down ~18-20% in past 1-3 months despite constructive pricing data.

bullets.title: TSM/AI capex cycle: TSMC hiking prices all nodes in 2027; CoWoS severely constrained; Q4 DRAM +20% QoQ
bullets.body: JPM notes TSMC will hike prices across all nodes in 2027 (vs. leading-edge only in 2026); 3nm, 2nm, and CoWoS capacity severely constrained in Q3 with Nvidia and Apple dominating allocation. Q4 DRAM contract prices forecast +~20% QoQ, NAND flash +~30% QoQ as AI server demand absorbs capacity. Asia Tech top picks include TSMC.

bullets.title: BURL: GS bullish on share gains and long-term margin expansion; PT $382
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs is confident in Burlington's share gains, localization, supply-chain productivity, and long-term margin expansion, with a price target of $382.

bullets.title: FSLR: ROTH bullish on solar/EPC sector; behind-the-meter ~70% of mandates as datacenter power drives demand
bullets.body: ROTH maintains bullish stance on solar/EPC sector including FSLR. Behind-the-meter configurations now represent ~70% of mandates; buildable land has moved ahead of power as near-term constraint. Political backlash against datacenters creates timing risk to 2027 US project starts.

bullets.title: RBLX: Roth launching cohort survey on user aging and bookings per user (Vol. 13)
bullets.body: Roth Capital's Volume 13 survey (n=1,000) tracks Roblox user engagement, cohort spending, churn to Fortnite/Minecraft, and aging-up thesis. Results could be a near-term catalyst for the aging-up debate. Standard pricing $5,000; first-time trial $3,500.

bullets.title: $6.9tn options expiry Sept 18: triple-witching with above-average single-stock volumes (20% above YTD)
bullets.body: Citi flags $6.9tn notional open interest expiring Sept 18 — the largest September expiry on record — split $5tn indices, $952bn ETFs, $998bn single-stock. Single-stock options volumes are 20% above YTD average; 2026 witching-day volatility has been above historical norms. 50 chains flagged with strikes within ±2% of price vs. elevated open interest.
